about: CM step 2 batch 4 (census Q12, harness gap H1): what the favorites list is after a rename, a merge or a title:: change that renames a page. Each scenario is a small graph, one operation and the one answer (`target`), set by the manager's rulings (FAV-MERGE, FAV-ALIAS, f3, FAV-RETITLE; see the design note cm-step2-favorites-design.md and `ruling` on a scenario). One answerer computes it: tine-graph-features `pages::commit_config` (the rename's config step, and `pages::follow_page_identity` after a title:: change). Three entries run every scenario and record where they differ from `target` in expected-differences.json: `rust` (`pages::rename_or_merge_page`, or a guarded page write plus `follow_page_identity` for a retitle), `owner` (the headless CLI owner, `tine serve`: no window, so no TypeScript runs; `page.rename`, or `block.edit` of the title for a retitle) and `frontend` (src/cmFavoritesRename.test.ts: the window adopts the backend's answer and computes and writes nothing itself). Names avoid the owner test graph's seed pages (a, b, ns, ns/child, dup).

scenarios.about: A favorite page is renamed; another favorite stays.
scenarios.og: rename-page-aux: unfavorite-page! old, favorite-page! new-page-name (lower-cased, moved to the front): ["omega" "Other"]

scenarios.about: The favorite is stored under another case spelling of the renamed page.
Renaming a namespace parent moves its descendants; a favorite descendant follows too.
scenarios.og: rename-namespace-pages! calls rename-page-aux for every namespace page, so each favorite follows: ["work" "work/child"] (front-insertion order)
scenarios.ruling: f3: namespace children's favorites follow, as OG does.

scenarios.about: A favorite page is merged into an existing page that is not a favorite.
scenarios.og: merge-pages! does not call rename-page-aux; delete! of the source calls unfavorite-page!: ["Other"]
scenarios.ruling: FAV-MERGE: the merged-away page's favorite moves to the survivor (a favorite behaves like a link, and merge rewrites links, M-Q4). Deliberate OG difference: OG drops it (merge-pages! -> delete! -> unfavorite-page!).

scenarios.about: Both the merged-away page and the survivor are favorites: one survivor favorite remains, in the survivor's place.
scenarios.ruling: FAV-MERGE: moved to the survivor, deduplicated when the survivor is already a favorite.

scenarios.about: The favorite is stored under an alias of the renamed page. The alias stays declared in the moved file, so the stored spelling still opens the renamed page.
scenarios.og: favorited? compares the stored name with the old page name only; an alias spelling is not matched and stays: ["Al"]
scenarios.ruling: FAV-ALIAS: keep the stored alias spelling, as OG and the model's rename do with [[alias]] links (it still opens the page). Before this batch the TypeScript rewrote it to the new page name.

scenarios.about: A favorite with no file, only references, is renamed (the rename repoints its references).
scenarios.og: rename-page-aux requires a page entity; a referenced name is a page in OG's DB, so it follows: ["spirit"]

scenarios.about: The renamed page is both the home page and a favorite: both follow, in one config.edn write.
A favorite listed on the Favorites arrangement page is renamed: the page's link and :favorites follow.
The Favorites arrangement page itself is renamed: :tine/favorites-page follows it.
A title:: change renames the page (the file stays): its favorite and the home page follow, from the same answerer as a rename.
scenarios.ruling: FAV-RETITLE: a title:: change that changes the page's name moves its favorites and home through the Rust answerer (pages::follow_page_identity); no TypeScript computation. Not an I-12 exception.
scenarios.og: OG does not rename on a title:: property edit (rename! runs only from the page-title UI): ["Alpha" "Other"]

scenarios.about: A title:: change to another spelling of the same name keeps the stored favorite spelling (one favorite identity; D11).
